'''Tito Arecchi''' (11 December 1933 – 15 February 2021) was an Italian physicist who made significant contributions to laser physics and [[quantum optics]].

==Biography==
Arecchi graduated from the [[Polytechnic University of Milan]] in 1957 with a degree in electrical engineering. He became an assistant professor at the [[University of Milan]] in 1963 and a physics professor at the [[University of Pavia]] in 1970. From 1975 until his retirement in 2008, he was a physics professor at the [[University of Florence]]. He also served as a guest professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1969 to 1970 and was invited to [[IBM]] research laboratories in [[San Jose, California|San Jose]] and [[Zürich]].

He and [[Rodolfo Bonifacio]] independently derived the equations known as [[Maxwell–Bloch equations|Maxwell-Bloch equations]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Arecchi |first1=F. |last2=Bonifacio |first2=R. |date=1965 |title=Theory of optical maser amplifiers |journal=IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics |language=en |volume=1 |issue=4 |pages=169–178 |doi=10.1109/JQE.1965.1072212 |bibcode=1965IJQE....1..169A |issn=0018-9197}}</ref> 

Arecchi was President of the {{ill|Istituto nazionale di ottica|it|lt=National Optical Institute}} from 1975 to 2000.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fox.ino.it/home/arecchi/|title=Fortunato Tito Arecchi|work=Istituto Nazionale di ottica|language=Italian}}</ref> In 1995, he was awarded the [[Max Born Award]] by [[The Optical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/maxborn/|title=Max Born Award|work=The Optical Society}}</ref> In 2006, the [[Italian Physical Society]] awarded he and Giorgio Careri the Premio Enrico Fermi for their contributions to the study of radiation and matter. 

Arecchi died from a fall in [[Florence]] on 15 February 2021, at the age of 87.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://firenze.repubblica.it/cronaca/2021/02/16/news/firenze_e_morto_tito_arecchi_pioniere_dei_laser_universita_docente-287786913/|title=Firenze, è morto Tito Arecchi: fisico, pioniere dei laser|date=16 February 2021|work=La Repubblica|language=Italian}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/obituaries/f_tito_arecchi_v/|title=In Memoriam: F. Tito Arecchi V, 1933-2021 |date=15 February 2021 |website=osa.org| language=English}}</ref>

==Articles==
*''Instabilities and Chaos in Quantum Optics'' (1987)
*''I simboli e la realtà'' (1990)
*''Optical chaos (selected papers on)'' (1994)
*''Lexicon of Complexity'' (1996)
*''Determinismo e Complessità'' (2000)
*''Caos e Complessità nel Vivente'' (2004)
*''Coerenza, Complessità, Creatività'' (2007)
